children: Malta’s annual inflation rate edged down to 2.0% in August 2026 from 2.1% in the previous month.

Prices increased at a softer pace in food and non-alcoholic beverages (1.6% vs 1.7% in July), furnishings and household equipment (1.1% vs 2.9%), restaurants and hotels (2.9% vs 3.3%), and insurance and financial services (0.7% vs 1.0%), while they remained unchanged for alcoholic beverages and tobacco (1.8%), health (2.8%), recreation and culture (3.2%), education (3.2%), and miscellaneous goods and services (3.7%).
Costs in information and communication (-3.4% vs -1.6%) also declined further.
Meanwhile, prices rebounded in clothing and footwear (1.6% vs -3.6%), while they continued to increase in transportation (2.3% vs 1.9%) and housing and utilities (3.1% vs 3.0%).
On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.6% in August, following a 0.5% increase in the previous month.

title: Malta Inflation Edges Down in August
